headline: RBA holds rates at 4.35% for a second straight meeting as the Middle East crisis keeps oil elevated and your US holdings had a strong night.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Best mover in your portfolio last night — up 2.87% in the US session. GTA 6 hype is building momentum: the CEO teased more trailers following a Netflix streaming event, and Rockstar has been signalling its streamer launch strategy. The long-term thesis here is still squarely about GTA 6, and the market is warming up to it.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Another solid session last night, up 1.21% to $506. Recent earnings beat expectations with strong AI-driven Azure cloud growth, and the market continues to reward Microsoft's early lead in embedding AI across its products. Up 14.2% on your total investment.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Nudged up 1.1% today on the ASX — a nice tailwind from the broader AI sentiment and news flow around Meta's new open-source model and Google's Gemini updates. Still sitting 12.2% below your cost base though, so a recovery is underway but not complete yet.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Up 0.67% last night to $355.84. Google Cloud revenue grew 82% year-over-year according to Motley Fool analysis, which is making the case that Alphabet's massive capital spending on AI infrastructure is starting to pay off. Up 15.7% on your investment.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: A quiet positive session today, up 0.13%. Singapore lifted its 2026 growth forecast citing the AI boom and a resilient global economy — good news for emerging markets exposure broadly.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: Edged up slightly today on the ASX, reflecting last night's broadly flat US market. The S&P 500 and NASDAQ dipped marginally, so VTS holding steady is a fine result.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Unchanged today at $78.03 — no news, no drama. A diversified fund like this tends to smooth out the daily noise, which is exactly what you want from it.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Dipped 0.85% today to $4.68 — still the portfolio's weakest performer at -30.6% overall. Broader lithium market headwinds continue with analyst commentary today noting uncertain development outlooks across lithium stocks. No signs yet of a structural turnaround in lithium pricing.

watch_today.title: RBA holds at 4.35% — no relief yet for borrowers
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank kept rates on hold for a second straight meeting today in a unanimous decision. But they've left the door open to further hikes if inflation doesn't behave. Some economists are calling this 'disastrous' and urging another rise. For your portfolio, a steady rate environment is generally supportive of equities — nothing to act on here, but worth watching ahead of the next meeting.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 hype building, hold and enjoy the ride
watch_today.detail: Take-Two was your best mover last night (+2.87%). The CEO is teasing more GTA 6 trailers after a Netflix streaming event, and Rockstar appears to be lining up a major streamer launch strategy. The long-term bull case for TTWO is almost entirely GTA 6 — if the launch goes well, this stock has significant upside from here. You're up 9.2% overall. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: MSFT — strong AI momentum, hold confidently
watch_today.detail: Microsoft hit $506 last night, up 1.21%, and is now 14.2% above your cost base. A recent earnings beat driven by AI-powered Azure cloud growth has the market firmly behind this one. Zuckerberg's new AI push (Meta's open-source model) may intensify competition, but Microsoft's deep enterprise AI integration is a durable moat. No reason to do anything but hold.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — lithium pain continues, but no panic needed
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals slipped again today (-0.85%) and sits 30.6% below what you paid. Lithium market headwinds are real and ongoing — analyst commentary today flagged uncertain development outlooks across the sector. The long-term EV transition story hasn't changed, but the timeline for lithium prices recovering is unclear. For a long-term holder, selling now locks in the loss. Hold and monitor the lithium price cycle.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI sentiment improving, recovery underway
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF bounced 1.1% today and is slowly clawing back from its -12.2% overall loss. Today's AI news flow (Meta open-source model, Google Gemini updates, Singapore raising growth forecasts on AI) is broadly supportive. For a long-term holder, this is exactly the kind of ETF you buy and forget about. Hold.

watch_today.title: Oil up 2% — keep an eye on Middle East tensions
watch_today.detail: Crude oil jumped 2% last night to $83.78 a barrel as Middle East tensions remain elevated. Multiple major airlines (Air Canada, Air France, Scoot) have extended flight suspensions over the region. Higher oil feeds into inflation, which could complicate the RBA's rate decisions and weigh on consumer stocks. No direct action needed, but worth watching.

world.summary: The Middle East dominates global headlines as the US-Iran standoff deepens, oil prices surge, and airlines extend flight suspensions. Meanwhile Singapore lifts its growth outlook on AI optimism.

stories.title: The Middle East may be entering a post-American era as Trump's strategy unravels
stories.why_it_matters: Analysis from multiple major outlets suggests the US is losing its grip on the Middle East. Trump wants to disengage from the region but is being dragged back in — he's now demanding Iran pay war reparations, a provocative new demand with no clear diplomatic path. Reports also suggest Trump may be willing to walk away from the Iran conflict without securing a nuclear deal, which would leave the region in deep uncertainty. For everyday Australians, the knock-on effect is higher oil prices (crude jumped 2% last night) and continued global instability.

stories.title: Airlines extend Middle East flight suspensions as crisis deepens
stories.why_it_matters: Air Canada, Air France, and budget carrier Scoot have all extended their suspensions of Middle East flights as of today. This is a practical sign of just how serious the regional instability is — airlines don't pull routes lightly given the revenue cost. For travellers, it means limited options and higher fares on routes through or near the region. For markets, it signals the crisis isn't resolving quickly.

stories.title: Singapore raises 2026 growth forecast on AI boom and resilient global economy
stories.why_it_matters: Singapore has upgraded its economic growth forecast for 2026, explicitly crediting the AI boom and a stronger-than-expected global economy. This is a positive signal for Asian and emerging market investments — Singapore is seen as a reliable economic bellwether for the Asia-Pacific region. It's good background news for your VGE emerging markets ETF and broader global growth outlook.

stories.title: Trump asks Iran for war reparations in new escalatory demand
stories.why_it_matters: On top of the ongoing military standoff, Trump has now publicly demanded Iran pay war reparations — a highly unusual and escalatory diplomatic move. Iran has shown no indication it will comply, meaning this is likely to harden positions on both sides rather than open dialogue. The combination of no clear peace pathway and potential for further escalation is what's keeping oil elevated and markets on edge globally.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a quiet positive session today, up 0.19% to 9,250. Last night on Wall St, the S&P 500 and NASDAQ both dipped slightly — less than 0.1% and 0.3% respectively — so broadly flat. The big movers were oil (up 2% on Middle East tensions) and gold (up 1.27% to a massive $4,417/oz), both reflecting geopolitical anxiety. The Aussie dollar slipped slightly to US70.5 cents.

indicators.note: Essentially flat last night — a very mild dip.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Slight pull-back last night after recent strong runs.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Jumped 2% on Middle East tensions. Airlines suspending flights, no resolution in sight.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold hitting stratospheric levels — geopolitical anxiety and a weaker USD are driving this.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar eased slightly — down 0.17% to just over 70.5 US cents.

politics.summary: Two big stories out of Canberra today: the RBA held interest rates steady for a second meeting in a row, and the Albanese government is on the verge of getting its gambling reform bill through parliament after offering concessions to the Coalition.

stories.title: RBA holds cash rate at 4.35% — second consecutive pause, but warns more hikes possible
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia voted unanimously today to keep the official cash rate at 4.35% for the second meeting running. That means no relief yet for mortgage holders — your monthly repayments aren't changing. However, the RBA has kept the door open, warning they will hike further if inflation doesn't keep falling. Some economists are calling the hold 'disastrous' and pushing for another rise to truly kill off inflation. The next meeting will be closely watched.

stories.title: Albanese strikes deal with Coalition to pass gambling reform laws
stories.why_it_matters: Prime Minister Albanese has outlined a deal with the Coalition to pass the government's gambling reform legislation, including a new media code. The government has offered concessions — most notably agreeing to curb gambling inducements rather than a full advertising ban — to win Coalition support. For everyday Australians, this means tighter restrictions on gambling ads and promotional offers are coming, though the most sweeping proposals appear to have been softened to get the deal done.

ai.summary: The AI world is buzzing with Meta releasing a new open-source model, Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash proving highly competitive on benchmarks, and a remarkable moment where the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft united in asking Congress to mandate biosecurity screening for AI-generated DNA.

stories.title: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.2 as open-source — Zuckerberg doubles down on open AI strategy
stories.why_it_matters: Meta has made its Muse Spark 1.2 AI model fully open-source, meaning any developer or researcher can download, modify, and use it for free. Zuckerberg published what the Washington Post called a 'manifesto' arguing open AI development is essential for America. This is a direct challenge to OpenAI and Anthropic's closed model approach — by giving the technology away, Meta hopes to become the standard foundation that everyone builds on. For GXAI.AX holders, more open-source competition can accelerate AI adoption broadly, which is a tailwind for the sector.

stories.title: Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash lands just 2 points behind Claude Opus 4.7 at a third of the cost
stories.why_it_matters: Google's new Gemini 3.5 Flash model has landed on benchmarks (standard tests of AI capability) just 2 points behind Anthropic's top-of-the-line Claude Opus 4.7 — but at roughly one-third of the price to run. This is big for Alphabet: it signals Google is closing the gap with rivals on quality while winning on cost efficiency. For businesses choosing an AI provider, price-performance is everything, and Google is now a very compelling option. Positive signal for your GOOG holding.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft CEOs jointly ask Congress to mandate synthetic DNA screening
stories.why_it_matters: In an extraordinary show of unity from competing AI giants, the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft have jointly asked the US Congress to legally require all synthetic DNA (lab-made genetic material) orders to be screened by AI for potential bioweapon risks. The concern: as AI makes it easier to design dangerous pathogens, screening DNA synthesis orders is a key safety backstop. It's rare to see direct rivals align on anything — the fact they're all pushing this together suggests the biosecurity risk is considered very real.

stories.title: Bernie Sanders calls on Silicon Valley to pause AI development
stories.why_it_matters: US Senator Bernie Sanders has called on Silicon Valley companies to pause AI development, arguing the technology is advancing too fast without proper safeguards and could harm workers and society. Sanders is one of the most prominent voices to make this call publicly — though tech companies are unlikely to comply, it signals growing political pressure in Washington that could eventually lead to regulation. For investors in AI-exposed stocks like MSFT, GOOG, and GXAI.AX, regulatory risk is something to keep a long-term eye on.

sport.summary: NRL Round 24 team lists are out ahead of this weekend's action, with Broncos vs Warriors at Suncorp the headline Saturday night clash. Some interesting AFL trade and fixture news too.

stories.title: NRL Round 24 team lists confirmed — Broncos host Warriors at Suncorp Saturday night
stories.why_it_matters: Official team lists are now confirmed for Round 24. The blockbuster game for Gold Coast fans is Broncos vs Warriors at Suncorp Stadium on Saturday at 7:35 PM — Brisbane will be looking to keep their finals push on track. Round opens Thursday night with Panthers vs Roosters at CommBank, and the Titans head to Newcastle on Sunday at 2 PM. Storm are on their bye this week.

stories.title: PNG allowed to break NRL salary cap rule to sign Brian To'o from Panthers
stories.why_it_matters: A fascinating behind-the-scenes story: the PNG NRL franchise was granted a special exemption to exceed normal salary cap rules in order to sign Brian To'o from the Penrith Panthers. The NRL allowed PNG to break the standard cap rule — a concession designed to help the expansion club attract marquee Polynesian talent as they build their squad. It sets an interesting precedent for how the NRL treats expansion teams.

stories.title: AFL: AFLW 2026 pushes men's footy out of its most lucrative Sunday timeslot
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL has made the bold move of scheduling AFLW games in the prime Sunday afternoon timeslot, bumping men's AFL games out of what has traditionally been its most-watched and highest-revenue broadcast window. The decision is controversial — the league argues it's about growing the women's game, but critics say it risks cannibalising men's AFL ratings and revenue. The Age has a detailed breakdown of the reasoning and the pushback.

stories.title: Big Victorian club makes club-record offer to Zak Butters as AFL trade period heats up
stories.why_it_matters: A big Victorian club (unnamed in the headline but reported to be Geelong or Melbourne) has tabled a club-record financial offer to Port Adelaide midfielder Zak Butters, one of the game's most sought-after players. Butters is off-contract and this offer signals the trade period is about to get very interesting. Port Adelaide will be under enormous pressure to either match the offer or trade him for substantial draft capital.
